title: Instant previews while dragging
objective: Make a slider drag feel instant at Fit on photo-sized JPEG and RAW sources by rendering previews against a display-bounded proxy source through the existing compiled path, keeping the exact full-resolution render as a cancellable second phase for the histogram, the overlays and the 100% view, and removing the two 16 ms timers from the input-to-presented path, with the targets in the instant preview design measured on the M4 Mac.
context_summary: Today every slider input renders and uploads the full 24 to 60 MP frame and waits on a slider tick and a preview poll, so a frame lands 75 to 150 ms after its input and a wild drag shows values several frames late. The design renders the whole recipe against a proxy of the source sized to the photo area, which every current layer supports because orientation, crop, Basic and RAW development are resolution independent, and lets the exact phase be cancelled when a newer value arrives. The preview queue, the preview worker, the desktop's poll and slider driver, the evidence harness and the docs change; recipes, history, the API and exports do not.

tasks.description: Add the proxy source to the core: ProxyBounds, the separable area-average downscale of a SourceImage (linear light through the decode table, re-quantized through the threshold table) and of a LinearImage (planar f32 through its view), the proxy scale from the recipe's full-resolution output stage, the registry's proxy-eligibility rule (every layer at the source, colour or geometry stage), and the one-entry proxy cache keyed by source identity, proxy dimensions and bounds.
extra_context: Bounds are clamped to 4096 px per side and 8 megapixels; the proxy is refused (None, exact path) when the scale is 1 or larger. Proxy dimensions are round(width × s) × round(height × s) with a minimum of 1. The downscale runs on the shared Rayon pool above the one-megapixel threshold and serially below it, and never on the owner thread.

A RAW proxy is a LinearImage with the same fingerprint, an identity view and the averaged planes of the source's viewed region; its cache identity is the developed planes' allocation (storage_weak), so a white-balance redevelopment misses. A JPEG proxy keeps the fingerprint and the orientation field of its source.

No new full-frame allocation beyond the proxy itself, which is counted against the 512 MiB frame limit; the separable pass needs one intermediate of proxy_width × source_height × 3 f32 at most, bounded the same way.

acceptance_criteria: An integer-scale downscale of a synthetic JPEG equals the exact linear-light mean of each block re-quantized through the threshold table; a fractional scale's coverage weights sum to one per output pixel; a uniform image is unchanged at any scale; a RAW proxy through a cropped, oriented view equals the mean of the viewed planes.

The proxy scale is computed from the compiled full-resolution output stage of the recipe, so a rotated crop's proxy output fits the bounds, and bounds outside the limits are clamped rather than refused.
A recipe with a pixel-stage layer is ineligible and reported as such; the cache hits on the same identity, dimensions and bounds and misses on a resized window or a redeveloped RAW.
The performance-rules checklist is answered in the commit: which paths allocate, what bounds them, what runs on the pool, nothing on the owner.

steps: Add exact downscale tests against a hand-computed reference for 2×, 3× and a fractional scale on small synthetic fixtures, for both source kinds.
Add eligibility and cache identity tests through the registry and a fake bounds sequence.
Measure the 24 MP proxy build once in the release editor-performance diagnostic and record it in the commit message.
expected_results: Every downscale test matches its reference byte for byte or within one ulp for f32 planes; eligibility and cache behave as the design states.

tasks.description: Add cooperative cancellation to rendering: a shared cancellation token checked at chunk granularity by the exact transform pass, the resample pass, the streamed colour pass, the linear row pass and the histogram reducer, with a distinct cancelled error kind, so a superseded full-resolution render stops within about a millisecond without changing any pixel a completed render produces.
extra_context: The existing render, render_linear and reduce_raster signatures stay for every current caller; the cancellable variants take the token. A token that is never cancelled must not change any output byte: the existing exact tests are the proof.
A cancelled render returns the cancelled error, never a partial raster, and releases its scratch reservations.

acceptance_criteria: A 24 MP synthetic render cancelled from another thread after 5 ms returns the cancelled error within 10 ms of the cancel on the release profile, measured in a test that records the elapsed time.

The scratch budget's in-use figure returns to zero after a cancelled colour pass.

expected_results: Cancellation is prompt, output is unchanged when not cancelled, and no scratch leaks.

tasks.description: Make the preview job two-phase: PreviewRequest and PreviewJob carry optional ProxyBounds, the worker renders the proxy phase from the cached proxy source and sends it, then renders the exact phase (with the report when asked) under a cancellation token, and PreviewQueue cancels the active job's exact phase whenever a newer request supersedes it, stores the proxy source back into its cache, tags every result with its phase and proxy dimensions, and wakes the desktop through an optional waker callback after each send.
extra_context: One active job and one pending job remain the bound. A job whose stack is ineligible or whose scale is 1 has no proxy phase and behaves exactly as today. A truncated (layer_count) job never has a proxy phase and is never analysed, as today.

The exact phase of a cancelled job sends a result whose error is the cancelled kind so the desktop can count it; it never sends a partial raster. The queue drops any result whose generation is no longer current, as today.
EditorService::preview_job passes the bounds through; the owner still does no frame work. PreviewResult keeps its current fields and gains phase and proxy_dimensions.

acceptance_criteria: A job with bounds on an eligible stack yields two results under one generation, proxy first, and the proxy raster equals the exact recipe rendered against the exact downscale of the source byte for byte.
Requesting a newer job while an exact phase runs cancels that phase; the queue then yields only the newer generation's results, and the cancelled count is observable.
A job without bounds, with an ineligible stack, or truncated yields exactly one exact result as today, and the existing queue tests pass unchanged.
The waker is called once per sent result and never from the owner thread.

expected_results: Order, cancellation, fallback and exactness hold; no test relies on timing beyond a generous deadline.

tasks.description: Adopt the proxy in the desktop: derive ProxyBounds from the window, the open panels and the scale factor and send them with every preview request whose zoom fits them; upload and present the proxy phase; adopt the exact phase's report and retained raster without an upload at Fit; upload the retained exact raster on a zoom to 100% without re-rendering; derive the clipping overlay from the proxy raster while the exact phase is outstanding and mark it approximate; replace the 16 ms preview poll with the worker waker channel; send draft.set immediately when idle and remove the slider tick; extend the events, the state summary and the evidence settle rules.
extra_context: Every preview job site (refresh, preview_task, current_preview_task, crop_preview_task, draft_set_task) takes the bounds from one Editor method; a truncated crop-draft job keeps no proxy. At a percentage zoom whose displayed physical size exceeds the bounds, no bounds are sent.

preview_displayed carries proxy and proxy_dimensions; a new preview_exact_cancelled event counts superseded exact phases; the clipping_overlay events carry approximate; the state summary carries proxy: {eligible, dimensions, bounds}. Settle::SliderDraft and Settle::Preview wait for the proxy upload and, when the job asked for a report, for the exact phase's adoption, so every existing smoke and acceptance assertion about drafted histograms keeps its meaning.
The idle rule stands: with nothing in flight there is no timer for previews and no timer for the gesture. The waker is one channel subscription created once; the overlay worker uses the same one.

acceptance_criteria: The basic, basic-panel, basic-crop, basic-restart, histogram, workspace, crop, crop-draft, large24 and large60 smoke scenarios pass with every existing assertion, and their frames record proxy and proxy_dimensions.

editor-latency drag mode on 24 MP records every presented frame as a proxy of the fitted size and no full-resolution upload during the gesture; the exact phase of the last value is adopted and the histogram identity carries the draft revision.
A zoom to 100% after a committed frame uploads the retained exact raster with no preview job requested (the events show an upload and no render); a zoom back to Fit shows the proxy again.
No timer subscription exists while nothing is in flight, and a gesture opens no tick timer; the idle CPU measurement does not regress.
The performance-rules checklist is answered for every desktop message this touches.

Run the listed smoke scenarios with a fresh release build.

expected_results: Scenarios pass; frames and events show proxy presentation; the drained input-to-presented p95 at 24 MP is far below the previous 83 ms.

tasks.description: Extend the evidence harness for a wild drag: a paced slider step (interval_ms sends one value per interval through a gated timer that exists only while the step runs), an editor-latency burst mode (three seconds of exposure values at 120 per second sweeping -2 to +2 EV and back) reporting presented frames per second, the staleness of every presented frame and the largest gap between presented frames, proxy dimensions in every report and the new provisional targets in the verify timing summary.
extra_context: Staleness of a presented frame is its input's slider_draft_set time to its preview_displayed time, correlated by generation as the drag mode already does; a coalesced value that never reached the owner is counted, not measured. The report keeps every sample.
The target rows read the burst and drag reports through exact JSON paths like the existing targets and take the thresholds from the design's table.
The paced step lives in the desktop's evidence driver; its timer follows the idle rule and is gated on the step being active.
The burst analysis tolerates events without the proxy fields (it reports them as null) so it can run against the current binary; the proxy fields arrive with the desktop change.

tasks.description: Draw the photograph through a photo-surface primitive that owns its wgpu texture: an iced shader program whose prepare writes the raster handed to the view into a texture the pipeline keeps (recreated only when the dimensions change) and whose draw maps it into the widget bounds with the Fit containment or the exact percentage box, so a proxy frame reaches the screen in the redraw that follows the worker's wake and no image allocation round trip remains on the input path.
extra_context: The primitive draws whatever raster the canvas holds: the proxy at Fit and zoomed-out percentages, the exact raster at 100% and above. The clipping overlay and the crop draft keep the toolkit image path and stack over it. Bytes are reproduced exactly: the texture and the surface format match what the toolkit's image pipeline uses (sRGB-typed when the toolkit gamma-corrects), and a smoke capture of a flat fixture colour proves it.

preview_displayed is emitted when the raster becomes the surface's source and a redraw is requested, with the same fields as today; the design records that presented means that update. Uploaded is no longer part of the photo path.
One texture per surface plus the retained rasters already held; the write is one queue.write_texture per changed frame, never per redraw.
